issues: fin/api.py turns each HTTP request into CLI argv strings and calls cli.main, so the API depends on CLI parsing; a description containing ';' is rejected, and values starting with '-' can be misparsed.

fin/api.py `_handle` maps every CLI failure to 400, and `_cli` recovers the message by stripping the 'error: ' prefix from stderr, which is fragile; Unauthorized/Forbidden from inside the CLI call would come back as 400.
fin/cli.py `main` catches only UserError, so an unexpected exception such as a sqlite3 error, a corrupt database or a bad rule regex at run time ends in a traceback instead of exit code 2.

fin/invoices.py `_next_number` numbers invoices with COUNT(*) of the same-year prefix; this is fragile (any deletion or manual change would produce duplicate numbers) and relies on the UNIQUE constraint to catch the clash.

fin/documents.py `apply_payment`, fin/cli.py `Context.book_currency` and fin/imports.py `_book_account` each re-query or re-implement the book currency and account checks; `check_access` is also duplicated by `_role_of` and by `_authorize` in the API.
fin/reports.py `ledger` loads every posting up to the end date and filters in Python, and `aging` runs several queries per document, so these reports will scale badly.
strengths: Money handling is consistent: Decimal everywhere with half-up rounding in fin/money.py, a '0.00' normaliser, regex-validated parsing and parameterised SQL.

The design is modular: each command module registers its own parser and handlers, shared document logic for invoices and bills lives in fin/documents.py, and each CLI command runs inside a single transaction that rolls back on error.
The tests drive the real CLI through a shared helper (tests/support.py) with a fresh database per test, and check behaviour including error cases, numbering, rounding and partial payments.
